traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Pittosporaceae: leaves usually alternate, sometimes whorled; leaves simple; margins usually entire, sometimes serrate; veins pinnate; leaves evergreen; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, rarely polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers solitary, in cymes or in corymbs; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule or berry; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 2 (-5). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 435, 436, family Pittosporaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral (sometimes whorled at shoot tips), usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.
